Point_Coordinates.focus: Carry the existing black sphere and compare LOCAL with WORLD. Read what makes the body grabbable and how its position is expressed in each coordinate frame. The XR player setup is supplied; the pickable-body connection is part of this lesson. Distance calculation belongs in Point Lines.

Primitives_Godot.focus: Continue the carried PointBody sphere. While held, reduce its rings and radial segments in timed integer steps; release pauses, re-grab continues and reset restores. Stop at rings 1 and radial segments 4. Keep size, material and collider fixed; compare the two resolution settings separately. Carry a familiar object whose construction can change through interaction, on its way toward the catalyst.

subjects: Reusing the PointBody and its trace
A list index and a spatial address
Rounding at a chosen grid spacing
Comparing two rules on the same record
Point_Line_Grid.focus: Continue the tested PointBody recorder in the same unit-scale PointStudy. Derive integer XYZ addresses and green snapped positions from its local source array; keep pink source values and order. Compare 0.25 m and 0.50 m pitches on one retained gesture. No display fitting or cross-hall transport.

subjects: Saving the drawing for the next hall
Point_Trace.focus: Inside the Trace hall, retain local positions in metres with an array, minimum-distance condition and neighbour loop. Connect the existing release event to the supplied archive. Save the visible segments as a static sculpture with their position record; carry it to Grid in the same project.
